'''George Frederick Oster''' [[National Academy of Sciences|NAS]] (April 20, 1940 – April 15, 2018)<ref>[https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/george-f-oster-eu0nbq/ George F. Oster]</ref> was an American mathematical [[biologist]], and Professor of Cell and Developmental Biology at [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mcb.berkeley.edu/index.php?option=com_mcbfaculty&name=osterg|title=Faculty Research Page|work=berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnr.berkeley.edu/~goster/home.html|title=Oster Lab - At the University of California, Berkeley|work=berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ciber-igert.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/twiki/view/CiBERIGERT/Faculty|title=CiBER &#124; Center for Interdisciplinary Bio-inspiration in Education and Research}}</ref> He made seminal contributions to several varied fields including chaos theory, population dynamics, membrane dynamics and molecular motors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://santafe.edu/news-center/news/memoriam-george-oster|title=In memoriam: George Oster {{!}} Santa Fe Institute|website=santafe.edu|date=18 April 2018 |language=en|access-date=2018-11-03}}</ref> He was a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|1985 MacArthur Fellow]].

== Early career ==
He graduated from [[Columbia University]], with a Ph.D., in Nuclear Engineering in 1967.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://news.berkeley.edu/2018/04/20/george-oster-pioneer-in-applying-mathematics-to-biology-dies-at-77/|title=George Oster, pioneer in applying mathematics to biology, dies at 77|date=2018-04-20|work=Berkeley News|access-date=2018-11-03|language=en-US}}</ref> He was appointed as an assistant professor in at UC Berkeley in 1970.<ref name=":1"/> In the early 1970s Oster collaborated with [[Aharon Katzir|Aharon Katzir-Katchalsky]] on statistical mechanics.<ref name=":1" /> He also collaborated with Alan Perelson and [[Aharon Katzir|Aharon Katzir-Katchalsky]]  on Network Thermodynamics: the application of [[Bond graph|Bond Graphs]] to the [[thermodynamic modelling]] of [[Biophysics|biophysical systems]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Oster |first=George |last2=Perelson |first2=Alan |last3=Katchalsky |first3=Aharon |date=1971 |title=Network Thermodynamics |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/234393a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=234 |issue=5329 |pages=393–399 |doi=10.1038/234393a0 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Oster |first=George F. |last2=Perelson |first2=Alan S. |last3=Katchalsky |first3=Aharon |date=1973 |title=Network thermodynamics: dynamic modelling of biophysical systems |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/quarterly-reviews-of-biophysics/article/abs/network-thermodynamics-dynamic-modelling-of-biophysical-systems/77B431E57497AFE757A8597FA690AD4E |journal=Quarterly Reviews of Biophysics |language=en |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=1–134 |doi=10.1017/S0033583500000081 |issn=1469-8994|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Oster's work with [[E. O. Wilson]] on populations dynamics of social animals, particularly ants, is considered pioneering work in evolution in social insects.<ref name=":1" /> Oster was one of the first theoretical biologists to understand that a complex interplay between mechanical and chemical forces was at the root of most biological phenomena.<ref name=":1"/>

== Later career ==
He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nuzzo|first1=R.|author1-link= Regina Nuzzo |year=2006|title=Profile of George Oster|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=103|issue=6| pages=1672–1674| doi=10.1073/pnas.0509056103|pmc=1413643|pmid=16446440|bibcode=2006PNAS..103.1672N|doi-access=free}}</ref> Oster was a [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1975|Guggenheim Fellow]], and a member of the science board of the [[Santa Fe Institute]].<ref name=":1" />

==Awards==
*1975 [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]
*1984 [[MacArthur Fellows Program]]
*1992 [[Weldon Memorial Prize]]
*Winfree Prize for Mathematical Biology
*Sackler International Prize in Biophysics
